message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two Draw‑Two, two Reverse, two Skip). 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild‑Draw‑Four cards. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a Wild‑Draw‑Four, the next player draws four cards and skips a turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). On your turn you may:
1. **Play a card** that matches the color, number, or symbol of the top discard card, or play a Wild card.
2. **Draw a card** from the draw pile if you cannot or choose not to play. If the drawn card can be played immediately, you may do so on the same turn. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Draw‑Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild‑Draw‑Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk being challenged.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Draw‑Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild‑Draw‑Four = 50. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach 500 points (or your chosen target) wins. If you’re playing a single round, the highest scorer wins. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on the discard pile** – you can often anticipate what the next player will need to play. 2. **Use Wild‑Draw‑Four strategically** – it’s powerful but risky; use it when you’re sure you have no matching color. 3. **Plan your “UNO”** – if you’re about to finish, consider playing a special card that forces the next player to draw or skip, giving you a better chance to finish. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
